topic: RC Circuit: Charging, Discharging and Time Constant
title: RC Time Constant Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav's camera flash fires in a blink, then makes him wait a few seconds before it can fire again. Why? In this animated lesson we fill a water tank through a thin pipe, then build the same idea on a live breadboard: a 10 V battery, a resistor, a capacitor and a two way switch, with the oscilloscope drawing the capacitor voltage and the current as the capacitor charges and then discharges.

We see why the filling slows down (the 10 V is shared by the resistor and the capacitor), meet the time constant tau = RC, and learn the 63% rule: after one tau the capacitor is about 63% charged, and after five tau it is practically full. Then the charging and discharging formulas step by step, why RC is in seconds, a worked example (10 kΩ and 220 μF give tau = 2.2 s), the exam trap, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 34 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 5: Application of D.C and A.C to Passive Components (Karnataka I PUC Electronics). RC charging and discharging is also asked in JEE Main.
